chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Sama'ah from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about the Muqim (resident of Makkah), is it for him to perform Tamattu' with the Umrah until the Hajj? He said: Yes. He goes out to the boundary of his land, so he pronounces the Talbiyah if he wishes.

key_terms.إِنْ شَاءَ: If he wishes, indicating permissibility rather than obligation for this specific method
key_terms.التَّمَتُّع: Tamattu', a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah and then Hajj separately, entering Ihram for each
key_terms.الْمُجَاوِر: The Muqim, a resident of Makkah who performs Hajj in their local state without entering Ihram from outside
key_terms.مُهَلِّ أَرْضِهِ: The boundary or outskirts of the land/city, the point where one exits the urban area to assume Ihram
key_terms.يُلَبِّي: Pronounces the Talbiyah (the ritual declaration: 'Labbayk Allahumma Hajj')

ai.seo_question: Can a resident of Makkah perform Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the specific ritual procedure for the Muqim (resident of Makkah) to perform Hajj al-Tamattu', requiring them to exit the city limits to a visible boundary (Muhill) before assuming Ihram. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical transition from the state of residence to the state of pilgrimage, ensuring the distinct legal status of the Umrah and Hajj seasons. It reflects the practical application of Quranic injunctions regarding the sanctity of the Haram and the conditions for valid pilgrimage rites.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Sama’at, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the one in the vicinity (of Makkah), is it for him that he should perform Tamatto with the Umra to the Hajj?’
Heasws said: ‘Yes. He should be going out to a place of its land, so he should be exclaiming Talbiyya if he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who resides in Makkah: if he can perform al-‘Umrah of al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘
(advantageous). He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so. He goes out to a Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram) to say Talbiyah, if he likes.’”
